analysis.investment_thesis: Cupid Limited is a niche condom/diagnostics manufacturer trading at an obscene 166x P/E and 150x EV/EBITDA for a business delivering a paltry 5.3% revenue CAGR — this is the definition of a speculation trap masquerading as a growth story. At 13,872 Cr market cap against 183 Cr revenue and 41 Cr net profit, there is zero margin of safety and almost no plausible earnings path that justifies the current price.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet — D/E of just 0.07 and 59 Cr cash with minimal borrowings (27 Cr)
Exceptional gross margins at 62% indicate strong pricing power in its niche export/government tender market
Export diversification across Africa, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and LatAm reduces India-specific demand risk
key_risks: Catastrophic valuation — P/E 166x and EV/EBITDA 150x for a business growing revenue at 5.3% CAGR and operating income at just 0.6% CAGR; no growth rate can justify this
Free cash flow turned deeply negative (-31 Cr FCF in FY2025) despite 41 Cr net profit — severe working capital deterioration and poor earnings quality
Government tender dependency for condom business creates lumpy, unpredictable revenues with zero pricing power; Other Income jumped from 0 to 19 Cr in FY2025, masking core business stagnation
red_flags: Revenue CAGR of 5.3% and operating income CAGR of 0.6% over 4 years — this is NOT an India growth story at any valuation, let alone 166x P/E
OCF swung from +42 Cr (2021) to -11 Cr (2025) while net profit rose — massive earnings-to-cash divergence is a serious quality red flag
Institutional ownership near zero (FII 1.01% + DII 0.17% = 1.18%) on a ~7,000 Cr+ market cap company signals smart money is absent entirely
Promoter holding at 46.03% — below my 50% comfort threshold and could dilute further given recent fundraising (99 Cr financing CF in FY2024)
Other Income surge (0 → 19 Cr in FY2025) inflating reported EBITDA margins; strip it out and core operating profit is actually declining
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cupid Limited fails my most fundamental test: I want to buy growth at a reasonable price, and this business offers neither. Revenue grew from 149 Cr to 183 Cr over four years — a meagre 5.3% CAGR that doesn't even keep pace with India's nominal GDP growth. Operating income in FY2025 (42 Cr) is barely above FY2021 levels (41 Cr) — four years of zero operating leverage. Yet the market has assigned a 166x P/E multiple, which would be stretched even for a company compounding at 25% annually. The condom and diagnostics space is dominated by government procurement tenders — this is NOT a consumer franchise with pricing power; it is a commodity supplier to public health programs.

The cash flow deterioration is deeply troubling. A business earning 41 Cr in reported net profit should be generating cash — instead OCF is -11 Cr and FCF is -31 Cr in FY2025. Something is consuming working capital aggressively. The balance sheet expansion from 189 Cr (2023) to 442 Cr (2025) total assets, financed by a 99 Cr capital raise, suggests the company is building capacity — but for what demand, given flattening revenues? ROE at 12.9% is below my 15% minimum. Promoter holding has slipped below 50% with near-zero institutional validation. I would not touch this at 20x earnings, let alone 166x. This is a pump story, not an investment.
